coverage: All three parts, both English editions: named cast, distinct recognizable unnamed roles and communities, family references, the book author and cultural allusions. Exact selected references, not blanket pronoun/ethnic-label matching.

entities.name: Charlie Marlow
entities.body: The seaman whose journey into Central Africa forms the main story.

entities.name: Mr. Kurtz
entities.body: The Company’s leading ivory agent, based at the Inner Station.

entities.name: The frame narrator
entities.body: One of the men aboard the Nellie, listening to and recounting Marlow’s story.

entities.name: The Director of Companies
entities.body: The captain and host of the gathering aboard the Nellie.

entities.name: The lawyer
entities.body: One of Marlow’s companions aboard the Nellie.

entities.name: The Nellie’s accountant guest
entities.body: The accountant listening to Marlow aboard the Nellie.

entities.name: Marlow’s aunt
entities.body: Marlow’s aunt, who uses her connections to help him obtain the river command.

entities.name: Fresleven
entities.body: The Danish steamboat captain whom Marlow replaces.

entities.name: The village chief
entities.body: The village leader involved in Fresleven’s dispute over hens.

entities.name: The chief’s son
entities.body: The son of the village chief in the account of Fresleven’s quarrel.

entities.name: The older knitting woman
entities.body: The older woman at the Company’s European office, watching the visitors.

entities.name: The younger knitting woman
entities.body: The woman at the Company’s European office who guides visitors into the waiting room.

entities.name: The secretary
entities.body: The secretary who handles Marlow’s visit and paperwork at the Company’s European office.

entities.name: The Company’s head
entities.body: The senior Company official who receives Marlow at the European headquarters.

entities.name: The young clerk
entities.body: The Company employee who escorts Marlow to his medical examination.

entities.name: The Company doctor
entities.body: The doctor who examines recruits before they leave for Africa.

entities.name: The Swedish captain
entities.body: The captain of the small coastal steamer that carries Marlow to the Company station.

entities.name: The Swedish traveler
entities.body: The man mentioned by the Swedish captain in his account of the journey inland.

entities.name: The chained laborers
entities.body: The African workers forced to carry loads while chained together near the station.

entities.name: The guard
entities.body: The armed African guard accompanying the chained laborers.

entities.name: The young worker in the grove
entities.body: The severely weakened young African worker whom Marlow approaches under the trees.

entities.name: The Company’s chief accountant
entities.body: The Company bookkeeper at the first station Marlow visits.

entities.name: The accountant’s laundry worker
entities.body: The African woman who maintains the accountant’s linen.

entities.name: The sick agent
entities.body: The ill Company agent placed in the accountant’s office.

entities.name: The road official
entities.body: The European official Marlow meets on the overland route, claiming responsibility for the road.

entities.name: Marlow’s traveling companion
entities.body: The European man accompanying Marlow on the overland journey to the Central Station.

entities.name: The Central Station manager
entities.body: The Company official in charge of the Central Station, overseeing the upriver expedition.

entities.name: The manager’s young servant
entities.body: The young African servant employed by the Central Station manager.

entities.name: The man blamed for the fire
entities.body: The African man accused of causing the fire at the Central Station.

entities.name: The brickmaker
entities.body: The Central Station agent assigned to make bricks, closely aligned with the manager.

entities.name: The boilermaker
entities.body: The mechanics’ foreman who works with Marlow on repairing the steamboat.

entities.name: The manager’s uncle
entities.body: The leader of the Eldorado Exploring Expedition and uncle of the Central Station manager.

entities.name: The Eldorado Exploring Expedition
entities.body: The expedition led by the manager’s uncle in search of wealth in the interior.

entities.name: The pilgrims
entities.body: Marlow’s ironic name for the European Company agents.

entities.name: The African crew
entities.body: The African men hired to work aboard Marlow’s steamboat, whom he calls cannibals.

entities.name: The crew’s headman
entities.body: The leader of the African crew working aboard Marlow’s steamboat.

entities.name: The fireman
entities.body: The African crewman tending the steamboat’s boiler.

entities.name: The helmsman
entities.body: The African crewman who steers Marlow’s steamboat.

entities.name: The poleman
entities.body: The crewman measuring the depth of the river from the steamboat’s bow.

entities.name: Towson or Towser
entities.body: The author of the seamanship manual Marlow finds; Marlow is unsure of the surname.

entities.name: The Russian trader
entities.body: The young independent trader in patched clothes, an admirer of Kurtz.

entities.name: The Russian trader’s father
entities.body: The arch-priest from the Tambov region whose son is the young trader.

entities.name: Van Shuyten
entities.body: The Dutch trader who supplied the young Russian for his journey.

entities.name: Kurtz’s Intended
entities.body: Kurtz’s fiancée, living in Europe.

entities.name: Kurtz’s mother
entities.body: Kurtz’s mother, described as half-English.

entities.name: Kurtz’s father
entities.body: Kurtz’s father, described as half-French.

entities.name: Kurtz’s African companion
entities.body: The African woman closely associated with Kurtz at the Inner Station.

entities.name: The Company’s representative
entities.body: The official who visits Marlow in Europe to claim Kurtz’s papers for the Company.

entities.name: Kurtz’s cousin
entities.body: The man who identifies himself as Kurtz’s cousin and describes his musical gifts.

entities.name: The journalist
entities.body: The journalist who knew Kurtz and discusses his public speaking with Marlow.

entities.name: Sir Francis Drake
entities.body: The English seafarer associated with the Golden Hind.

entities.name: Sir John Franklin
entities.body: The British naval explorer associated with the Erebus and Terror.

entities.name: Elizabeth I
entities.body: The English queen who visited Drake’s Golden Hind.

entities.name: The Buddha
entities.body: The Buddhist spiritual teacher invoked in comparisons with Marlow’s seated pose.

entities.name: Plato
entities.body: The ancient Greek philosopher named in the young clerk’s remark.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: The Roman god of war, invoked in Marlow’s ironic imagery.

entities.name: Mephistopheles
entities.body: The devil figure of the Faust story, used in Marlow’s comparison of the brickmaker.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: Another name for Jupiter, the Roman chief god, invoked in oaths and imagery.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The divine being invoked in religious expressions and oaths.
